I am 43 years old and I have farmed this land for 20 years. I never went to school, so I cannot read the labels on fertilizer bags very well — I recognize them by the color and the pictures, and I ask the man at the county supply store to confirm. My husband works construction in Handan and sends money home, but it is not much, so I must be careful. My daughter is in middle school and my mother-in-law lives with us. Mostly it is me and my mother-in-law doing the farm work, but her back is bad now, so I hire help for planting and harvest days.

We have 12 mu and we grow wheat then maize, same as every household in our village. I would never change this — it is what my mother-in-law did, and what her mother-in-law did. The soil is tired after the maize, so for the winter wheat I will rotary till the field after cutting the corn stalks, then broadcast the wheat seed and fertilizer by hand and drag a wooden plank to cover them. I use the same wheat seed I always buy from the county store — it is not the fancy kind, but it is improved and I know it. I will put down compound fertilizer before planting, about one big bag for every two mu, and then in March at jointing I will topdress with urea. I never skip the topdressing. Three years ago I tried to save money and the wheat was so thin I lost two hundred jin per mu. My neighbor Auntie Wang did the same thing two years ago and she cried at harvest. I irrigate wheat three times — green-up, jointing, and grain filling — because wheat is our main food and the well is there. I spray herbicide once because the weeds get bad in spring.

For summer maize, the window is so tight. Sometimes we only have two days between wheat harvest and planting. I buy new hybrid maize seed every year — you cannot save maize seed, everyone knows that. I do one quick pass with the rotary tiller if the stubble is thick, then plant fast with the machine I hire from the village. All the fertilizer goes in at planting — about 30 kg of compound fertilizer and a bit of urea in the furrow — because there is no time for split application. The season is too short. I irrigate maize twice if the summer is dry, but often the July rains help. I spray twice — once for weeds and once for insects, because the corn borer came bad in 2019 and the ears were half empty. I still remember that.

I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a bad year. We need about 5,500 yuan for inputs, which is a lot, but my husband sends some and we have a little saved. Better to eat less meat now than to starve at harvest.
